task.prompt: Explain population variance to someone who knows averages but no statistics.
task.oracle: Population variance of [1,3] is 1, mean2, squared units; sample unbiased variance2 for n=2. Squaring is not uniquely forced by avoiding cancellation.
task.reference: Population variance measures spread that an average alone hides. Assume the complete population is [1,3]; it has mean 2, just like [2,2], but only the first pair is spread out. Its deviations are -1,+1; squared deviations average to (1+1)/2=1 in squared units. Dividing by n-1 instead estimates population variance from a sample; squaring emphasizes large deviations, rather than being the only possible spread measure. Keep the mean and population size fixed and change the distance from the mean: [0,4] gives (4+4)/2=4. Two machines may have the same average delivery time; comparing squared deviations of their complete delivery records reveals which is less consistent.

answer: 总体方差衡量一组数据离平均值有多分散。做法是：先求每个数与平均值的差，把差平方后求平均。平方能避免正负差互相抵消，并让较大的偏离受到更大权重。例如数据2、4、6的平均数是4，差为-2、0、2，平方为4、0、4，人口方差为8/3。方差越大，数据越不集中。

task.prompt: 给高中生讲解贝叶斯公式如何从阳性检测推到患病概率。
task.oracle: Teaching example prior1%, sensitivity90%, specificity90%; among1000 9 truepositive99 falsepositive, posterior9/108=8.33%. Not medical advice.
task.reference: 贝叶斯公式把阳性检测和原先患病比例合起来，回答阳性者中有多少真正患病。 假设1000人中10人患病，灵敏度和特异度都为90%；“病人测阳性的概率”与“阳性者患病的概率”方向不同。 10位病人中9人阳性，990位非病人中99人阳性，阳性者患病概率为9/(9+99)≈8.3%。分母合并所有阳性，分子只留患病阳性。 保持两项检测性能不变，只把患病比例改为50%，同样1000人有450个真阳性和50个假阳性，后验变为90%。 垃圾邮件过滤也把某个词在垃圾与正常邮件中的出现率和垃圾邮件先验合并；仅见到这个词还不能直接认定垃圾邮件。

answer: 阳性检测只说明“在患病和不患病的人中，阳性更常见”，不等于一定患病。贝叶斯公式把目标概率写成：P(患病|阳性)=P(阳性|患病)×P(患病)÷P(阳性)。例如患病率1%，检测灵敏度90%，未患病者假阳性率5%。每万人中约100人患病，其中90人阳性；9900人未患病，其中495人假阳性。因此阳性者共585人，真正患病的概率是90/585≈15.4%。患病率变低时，假阳性仍可能很多，阳性后的患病概率也会下降。

task.prompt: Explain cache invalidation in a web application to a beginner.
task.oracle: Stale cached copies after origin mutation; TTL vs explicit invalidation; distributed races and eventual freshness, do not claim perfect TTL consistency.
task.reference: Cache invalidation prevents an old saved result from outliving the change that made it wrong. Imagine a shop caching a product price: an unchanged price is a valid cache hit, but a hit after the database price changes can return stale data. The cache bypasses a database read; deleting or replacing its entry after a price update forces the next read to obtain the new price. A TTL only bounds staleness and does not synchronize all readers. Hold traffic and update timing fixed; shorten the TTL from ten minutes to one minute, reducing the stale window while increasing database reads. A DNS record also has cached copies and expiry: the same origin-change/copy-lifetime relation explains why an address change may take time to appear, though its protocol differs.

answer: A cache stores a copy of expensive-to-fetch data (like a user profile) so later requests are fast. Cache invalidation is the problem of keeping that copy correct when the underlying data changes. If a user updates their email but the cache still holds the old profile, users see stale data. Common strategies: TTL — expire entries after N seconds (simple, but briefly stale); write-through — update cache and database together on every write; delete-on-write — evict the key when data changes, so the next read refetches fresh data. It's hard because the cache and the source live on different machines: updates race with reads, failures leave copies inconsistent, and you must choose the right granularity. Hence the joke: "there are only two hard things in computer science: cache invalidation and naming things."

task.prompt: 讲解正反馈为什么会放大变化，以及为何不等于好事。
task.oracle: 反馈正负指方向不是好坏；环路有放大条件和饱和限制，增强不保证无限增长。
task.reference: 正反馈会把初始变化沿回路送回来继续增强，方向的“正”不代表好坏。 教学假设：麦克风拾取扬声器声音后再次放大；温度升高后空调加强降温则是反向作用。 声音经麦克风、放大器、扬声器再回到麦克风，若每圈回来的增量更大就增长；设备饱和会限制增长。 保持位置和音量输入不变，只降低环路增益到衰减区，啸叫会减弱而非持续放大。 传言引来关注、关注又扩大传言传播，也有同向回路；只有反馈足够强且未触及限制时才明显放大。

task.prompt: 用一个具体例子讲解相关与因果怎样区分。
task.oracle: Common cause, observational association insufficient, causal interventions need assumptions; icecream/drowning seasonal toy not actualdata.
task.reference: 相关表示一起变化，因果还要求一个变化能在合适条件下改变另一个。 假设夏天冰淇淋销量和溺水事件同时增加；这能体现相关，但共同的炎热天气可同时增加销量和游泳人数。 “炎热→销量”和“炎热→下水人数→溺水”两条路径足以产生一起上升，不需要冰淇淋导致溺水。 保持天气和下水人数固定，只减少冰淇淋销售；上述模型不会因此减少溺水，若真实结果不同还需重新检查模型与干预条件。 学校中课外阅读和成绩一起提高，也需检查家庭支持等共同原因；仅凭成绩相关无法确定阅读的因果效果。

answer: 相关只说明两个数字一起涨落，因果还要求「谁推动谁」。把相关当成因果，会开出无效的药方。例子：某城市统计发现，冰淇淋销量越高，溺水人数越多，两者高度相关。若据此禁售冰淇淋，溺水不会减少——因为真正的推手是第三个因素：天气热。天热让人既买冰淇淋又下河游泳，两者是同一原因的两个结果，这叫「混杂变量」；冰淇淋和溺水之间没有直接通道。另一种假因果来自方向颠倒：「消防员人数与火灾损失正相关」，不是消防员造成损失，而是大火招来更多消防员。判断因果需要能「改变一个，看另一个是否跟着变」：控制天气做对照，冰淇淋销量不同而溺水相同，因果链就断了。所以看到相关先问三件事：有没有共同原因？方向会不会反？是不是巧合？能设计干预实验时，答案才最硬。

task.prompt: 给没有机器学习背景的人讲解过拟合。
task.oracle: Low trainingerror not guaranteegeneralization; memorize noise, heldout leakage invalidates evaluation; no claim modelcomplexityalwaysbad.
task.reference: 过拟合会把训练样本里的偶然细节也记住，因此旧题表现好，新题可能变差。 假设模型预测房价；记住每栋训练房子的成交价可做到旧房零误差，学到面积等稳定关系则更有机会用于新房，零误差本身不能判定过拟合。 样本噪声并不稳定；模型用它减少训练误差时，新房不再有相同细节，预测便偏离。 保持模型和评估方式固定，只增加来自同一分布的独立训练样本，偶然细节更难支撑规则，过拟合风险通常下降，但不保证归零。 学生背答案而不会解新题也体现旧样本记忆和新情境应用的差别；这个类比不代表机器像人一样理解，新房评估仍要独立留出数据。

task.prompt: 讲解信息熵，说明为什么均匀概率通常更不确定。
task.oracle: H=-sum p log2p bits; faircoin1bit deterministic0; entropyofdistribution not individualsequence meaning/quality.
task.reference: 信息熵衡量一个概率分布下，结果尚未出现时平均有多不确定。 假设一枚公平硬币，正反各半；另一枚总是正面。两者都可能看到正面，但预测难度不同，熵描述分布而非某一次结果的意义。 H=-Σp log₂p：p是各结果概率，单位为比特。公平硬币算得-2×0.5×(-1)=1比特；确定结果为0，零概率项按极限取0。 保持两个可能结果固定，只把概率改成0.9和0.1，熵约0.469比特，因结果更易预测而降低。 明天只有“晴”“雨”两种教学假设时，也可用概率分布算预测不确定性；熵不衡量天气好坏或信息真假。
reference_parts: 信息熵衡量一个概率分布下，结果尚未出现时平均有多不确定。
假设一枚公平硬币，正反各半；另一枚总是正面。两者都可能看到正面，但预测难度不同，熵描述分布而非某一次结果的意义。
H=-Σp log₂p：p是各结果概率，单位为比特。公平硬币算得-2×0.5×(-1)=1比特；确定结果为0，零概率项按极限取0。
保持两个可能结果固定，只把概率改成0.9和0.1，熵约0.469比特，因结果更易预测而降低。
明天只有“晴”“雨”两种教学假设时，也可用概率分布算预测不确定性；熵不衡量天气好坏或信息真假。

answer: 信息熵衡量一次结果的不确定程度。若结果概率为p_i，熵为 H=-Σp_i log₂p_i，单位通常是比特。两面公平硬币的结果各为1/2，熵为1比特；若硬币几乎总是正面，观察结果前就容易猜中，熵较低。均匀分布通常更不确定，因为可能结果都同样合理，没有一个结果特别值得押注。注意这是“平均不确定性”，不是结果数量越多就必然越大；概率极不均匀时，新增的罕见结果贡献可能很小。

公式、各p、比特和两个1/2得到1的简单算例正确
同一硬币只变正面概率，说明更易猜且熵更低
没有表面不同的新场景迁移
补充平均含义和结果多不保证熵大，无实质事实错误

task.prompt: Explain deadlock with a small resource-allocation example.
task.oracle: Circularwaiting with exclusive locks and holdandwait, consistentordering breakscycle not allcontention; removingone process not alwaysglobalfailure.
task.reference: Deadlock occurs when waiting tasks prevent one another from making the progress needed to release resources. Assume task A holds exclusive lock X and waits for Y, while B holds Y and waits for X. One task waiting for a lock that another will soon release is ordinary contention, not this cycle. Neither can continue to its release step: A needs B’s resource and B needs A’s. The exclusive locks and hold-while-waiting rule sustain the cycle. Keep the two tasks and resources, but require both to acquire X before Y: B cannot hold Y while waiting for X, breaking this cycle while contention remains. Two trains occupying sections and each waiting for the other’s section can share the same exclusive-resource waiting cycle; actual railway rules determine whether that model applies.

answer: Deadlock is when processes each hold a resource and wait for the other's — so none can ever proceed. Small example: Transaction A locks row 1; Transaction B locks row 2. A then asks for row 2 while B asks for row 1. Each waits for the other to release, and neither ever will, because they only release after finishing. They wait forever. Four conditions must all hold: mutual exclusion (one holder per resource), hold-and-wait, no preemption (you can't take a lock away), and circular wait. Break any one and deadlock becomes impossible — which is where the fixes come from: acquire locks in a fixed global order (kills circular wait), request everything upfront (kills hold-and-wait), or time out and abort one victim. Notice the contrast with an ordinary wait: here waiting is mutual, so time doesn't help. A third transaction holding nothing can still run — deadlock starves its victims, not necessarily the whole system.

task.prompt: Explain Little’s law for an introductory queueing class.
task.oracle: L=lambda W stable longrun matchingboundaries units;2customers/min*3min=6; noPoissonneeded, waitingtimeversussystemtime match.
task.reference: Little’s law connects the average number in a stable system to the arrival rate and average time spent there. Assume a stable café averages two customer arrivals per minute and three minutes from entry to exit. Customers in the café and customers only waiting in line are different system boundaries. L=λW gives 2 customers/minute × 3 minutes = 6 customers on average. Each arrival contributes its residence time, so the long-run accumulated customer-time divided by observation time yields the same average occupancy; no Poisson assumption is required. Hold arrival rate and the stable café boundary fixed; reduce average residence to two minutes and L becomes four customers. Stable network requests in flight obey the same rate-times-latency relation, provided latency and request count refer to the same boundary and arrivals do not exceed sustainable service.

answer: Little’s law says: L = λW. Here, L is the average number of items in a system, λ is the average arrival rate, and W is the average time an item spends in the system. For example, if a café serves 10 customers per hour and each customer stays 0.5 hours on average, then L = 10 × 0.5 = 5 customers in the café on average. The law applies in a stable system over a sufficiently long period, regardless of the detailed service rule.
